subtitle: Metaphor and comparison, and how a speech is built
words.intro: At a German wedding somebody always gives a speech. It may begin in the registry office and go on through dinner. There is a newspaper written by the friends, and there is a game with a saw. A speech has a structure, and a metaphor has its own risks.

grammar[0].fact: German schoolchildren learn these terms by heart, and they’re tested on them in the Abitur: every German has at some time had to find an *Anapher* in a poem. So use them in speech, and someone in the room will notice. It may even be Dr. Brummer.

grammar[1].fact: A great German speech you could read is Richard von Weizsäcker’s, in 1985: it’s still studied, and it’s a model of long rhythm and plain words. It’s also a useful reminder that a good speech can do what no metaphor can: say something true in a room that doesn’t want to hear it.

document.intro: A real wedding newspaper, written by friends for Frida Strauß and Georg Kuhn in Charlottenburg, August 1919. It’s a parody of a famous satirical magazine, *Kladderadatsch*. Read the rhymes in the first week, and then the *Ehestandsregeln*. They are, shall we say, of their time.
document.fact: German friends still make these *Hochzeitszeitungen*, with old photos, jokes and rhymes. And look at the strip across the middle: *Dieses Blatt erscheint alle 25 Jahre einmal und kostet viel — Kopfzerbrechen.* That’s a real joke, with a set-up, a dash and a punchline, a hundred years old.

reading.intro: Vroni and Timo are getting married. He’s no longer her intern. Max is the best man, and he has spent a month on his speech. He’s used every device in this chapter. Dr. Brummer read it on Friday, and he didn’t say anything. He only took off his glasses.
reading.fact: German weddings have some customs you may not expect. On the *Polterabend* before the wedding, friends smash china outside the couple’s home, and the couple must clear up. After the ceremony, in some regions, the two saw through a log together. They do it to prove that they can, or that they should have thought harder.
